Title: Christianismi restitutio: totius ecclesiae apostolicae est ad sua limina vocatio, in integrum restituta cognitione Dei, fidei Christi, iustificationis nostrae, regenerationis baptismi, et manducationis Domini nostri Iesu Christi (reprint of the 1553 Vienne edition)
Creator: Michael Servetus (Miguel Servet); reprint issued by Christoph Gottlieb von Murr
Publisher: [Nuremberg]: Christoph Gottlieb von Murr, 1790 (as given in the host record)
Publication Date: 1790
Rights: Public Domain (published 1790; public domain by date; host licence Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0)
Language: lat
Source: Internet Archive item b28039427, file b28039427_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the library/source-research thread (Era VII session, one-world agent for anti-trinitarian-currents-servetus-polish-brethr), 2026-10-16; host rights statement: licenseurl http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/ (contributor Royal College of Physicians, London).
Provenance note: Header prepended; the OCR text follows unchanged apart from long-s to s normalisation (0 occurrences; most long-s is in fact read by the OCR as f, which was left as printed in the OCR). Rights basis restated: a 1790 reprint of a 1553 text is public domain by date, and the host marks the item Public Domain.
Content note: The whole reprint: some English bookseller's and owner's notes pasted in at the front, then the Latin Christianismi Restitutio in its books (De Trinitate divina in its Libri with two Dialogi from file line 9775, De fide et iustitia regni Christi from 13765, De caritate, then the four books on the heavenly regeneration and the kingdom of Antichrist headed De orbis perditione, De circumcisione, De ministeriis ecclesiae, De baptismi and De regeneratione, with a Conclusio at 27450 and the Epistolae to Calvin from 27483). OCR sampled at five points and found readable Latin with scattered errors (word-like share about 0.96); long-s is systematically read as f ('fupra' for 'supra'), so quote only after checking the page image. No public-domain English translation of the Restitutio exists.

Servetus  (lM  ) van  de  Dolinghen  in  de  Drievuldighevt  (de  Trini  A' 
tate),  blatit  letter,  red  morocco,  gilt-marbled  edges,  by  De  i

Prancesco  Stabili,  born  at  Ascoli,  and  better  known  as 
Ceccho  (the  diminutive  of  Francesco)  d’Ascoli,  was  the 
master  of  Dante,  and  in  later  years  his,  bitter  opponent. 
This  very  curious  work,  which  may  be  regarded  as  an 
Encyclopaidia  in  verse,  has  passed  through  numerous 
editions,  and  is  remarkable  as  supposed  to  contain  the 
discovery  of  the  circulation  of  the  blood.  The  author 
was  burnt  for  Heresy,  in  1327,  and  his  works  have  been 
strictly  prohibited  under  pain  of  excomraunication.
